name: X Buttons to Remove Chosen Founders
description: On the "Select 5 villagers" screen at the start of a new village, an X beside each chosen villager sends them away so you can pick another. Each X stands at the right end of that villager's name plank. Clicking it removes that villager for good, just as Reject does; the villagers chosen after them move along to fill the gap, and the candidate on show stays. Keep choosing until five are chosen. After the fifth pick, while the button says Done, an X takes you back to choosing: Select and Reject come back and a new candidate is shown. **Once the island has started, the five chosen are your founders and there are no X buttons.** The X buttons are the game's own stone button with an X on it. **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Seen working in a running game** (2026-11-24; bringing Select and Reject back after the fifth pick is checked by emulation and a test harness only). The companion is "VVFP Founder X Buttons.dll"; it never writes a save or a file.
behavior_changes: The "Select 5 villagers" screen (vtable 0x49A074; +8 the candidate's record, +0x18 the number chosen, +0x1C..+0x2C the five chosen records, +0x30 Reject) gets five buttons, ids 0x5858..0x585C, made as its Select and Reject are (the button constructor, the image manager's picture 0xCD btn_tech_question.png, the label "X" in Select's colours), each at the right end of its slot's name plank, just above it (slot x 202, 350, 503, 651, 803, plank top y 215). They are added to and removed from the screen (its own add / remove child calls) only in its draw (slot 6): one for each filled slot while a pick can change, none once five are chosen with Reject still on (the manager's flag +0x17E38 started the island).

Its command handler (slot 3, stock 0x43E600) takes an X click (8, 0x5858 + k): the chosen villager k's present byte (+0x1CD4) is cleared, as a Reject clears a candidate's; the later chosen move down one and +0x18 drops by one; the game's sound 0x66 (tap.ogg) plays. In the Done state (five chosen, Reject off) Select's label goes back to string 0x49 (as the screen's show sets it; string 0xDA is Done), Reject is added back in the next draw and 0x43E470 shows a new candidate. Every other message goes on to the stock handler.

The candidate generator 0x43E220 (its entry spliced): the candidate on show (+8) is freed when it is not chosen, and while the stock code runs +0x18 reads as the lowest record whose present byte is 0 -- where the game's allocator makes the candidate -- so the stock code frees, fills and returns that record (the stock screen counts on the candidate's record being +0x18); the real count is put back after. With no X used that record is +0x18 itself: the stock screen unchanged. The villager table is read from the generator's own `mov ecx` (0x43E22B) and records through the getter 0x46F950 until it returns none: 150 or 256 records.
explicit_non_changes: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes its three sites at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes and every routine it calls.
Select, Reject, the Done state, the start of the island (0x4259D0, which takes every present record as a founder) and the candidates themselves are the game's own.
A removed villager is gone as a rejected candidate is: no log calls it a disappearance (saves while this screen is open are not the village).
Nothing is written but the screen's chosen list and count and the removed villager's present byte; no file.

runtime_detours.routine: the candidate generator's entry (`sub esp, 10h / mov eax, [ecx+18h]`): the candidate on show freed unless chosen, +0x18 read as the lowest free record while the stock code runs
